definitions.explanation: Refusing to change one's mind, attitude, or position despite pressure or persuasion. Often carries a negative connotation of inflexibility, but can sometimes suggest admirable steadfastness.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{頑|かたく}なに{拒否|きょひ}した。
{頑|かたく}なな{態度|たいど}を{崩|くず}さず、{交渉|こうしょう}は{難航|なんこう}した。
examples.english: Negotiations struggled because they wouldn't budge from their stubborn stance.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{伝統的|でんとうてき}なやり{方|かた}を{頑|かたく}なに{守|まも}り{続|つづ}け、{最後|さいご}まで{手作業|てさぎょう}で{物|もの}を{作|つく}っていた。
examples.english: My grandfather stubbornly adhered to traditional methods and made things by hand until the very end.

notes:
USAGE:
{頑|かたく}な is a na-adjective. It is commonly used in the adverbial form {頑|かたく}なに to modify verbs meaning to refuse, insist, or maintain a position. It usually has a negative connotation (inflexibility), but context can make it positive (steadfast commitment).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {頑|かたく}なに{拒否|きょひ}する (to stubbornly refuse)
- {頑|かたく}なに{守|まも}る (to stubbornly protect/uphold)
- {頑|かたく}なな{態度|たいど} (a stubborn attitude)
- {頑|かたく}なな{姿勢|しせい} (a rigid stance)
- {頑|かたく}なに{否定|ひてい}する (to stubbornly deny)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頑|かたく}な: stubborn, rigid (refusing to change; often negative)
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn (strong-willed; can be positive or negative)
- {意固地|いこじ}: obstinate, perverse (childishly stubborn)
- {強情|ごうじょう}: headstrong, willful (refusal to yield)
